cross_revision_invariants.controller: GT911 on attached touch FPC/display module

shared_i2c.owner_policy: platform_i2c_shared is the sole bus owner; platform_touch borrows the bus and owns only its GT911 panel-IO device

existing_hardware_evidence.claim: A device at Elecrow's documented GT911 address acknowledged on I2C1 GPIO45/GPIO46 during D2.2
existing_hardware_evidence.claim_limit: An address ACK proves bus presence only; it does not prove coordinate reads, touch geometry, multi-touch, or the exact responding silicon

reset.policy: narrowly authorized for the pinned GT911 driver's active-low reset and address-latch sequence

interrupt.policy: narrowly authorized for the pinned GT911 driver's address latch and input mode; runtime is polling-only and registers no ISR callback

power.source: existing display/pad 3.3 V rail; platform_touch never acquires or releases a rail
power.cross_revision_note: V1.0/V1.1 name the pin LCD_VDD and V1.2 names it VDD_3V3; V1.0/V1.1 populate R65=0R between those nets, so the effective supply is 3.3 V in all revisions

revision_differences.safe_common_driver_policy: the pinned driver actively drives GPIO40 reset and GPIO42 low/high only during address selection, then leaves GPIO42 as an input with no ISR callback; polling does not depend on the unpopulated V1.1/V1.2 INT pull-up

reviewed_semantics: GPIO45 SDA and GPIO46 SCL on one caller-created shared I2C bus
active-low GPIO40 reset and GPIO42 interrupt/address latch
polling reads; no application dependence on a runtime interrupt
platform_differences: platform_touch bounds output to five contacts instead of the lesson's single contact
platform_touch deletes the failed primary panel-IO before creating the fallback device
platform_touch provides fail-closed frames and retryable cleanup ownership

reviewed_behavior: GT911 1.1.3 rejects controller-reported contact counts above five
the configured esp_lcd_touch core buffer is exactly five points
the public coordinate API returns at most the caller-provided maximum
GT911 1.1.3 polls status, bounds the point payload to 40 bytes, and clears the ready register
the public driver does not expose GT911 track IDs; consumers use set-union hit testing

authorization.rationale: The complete GT911 I2C, reset, interrupt/address-latch, power, and ground topology is equivalent across every published 10.1-inch revision. The pinned Elecrow Lesson05 source uses the same GPIO40/GPIO42 active-low address-selection sequence across V1.0/V1.1/V1.2. This grants a narrow build authorization only; a build is not hardware verification.
